main_topics.reason: The user came to understand the treatment landscape and repeatedly asked how clinicians choose among options.
The user called long-term risk their biggest fear, explored the risks of treatment versus active inflammation, and said the discussion reframed the decision.
The user described persistent hand and wrist synovitis, elevated CRP, and prolonged morning stiffness as the reason escalation was being considered.
The user asked whether recurrent sinus infections and prior shingles should steer the choice of treatment.
The user asked whether Shingrix was appropriate at their age and while immunosuppressed, then added it to their appointment questions.
The user discussed frequent work travel and asked how self-injections, infusions, and oral options differ in practice.
The user asked how long it takes to know whether a biologic is working and wanted to avoid months of uncertainty and pain.
The user asked whether possible hormone therapy during perimenopause could interact with RA treatment.
The user briefly said they were needle-shy despite already using injectable methotrexate.

output.summary: The user wanted to prepare for a rheumatology appointment about adding a biologic for active RA despite methotrexate and sulfasalazine. The assistant discussed treatment classes, infection and shingles history, vaccination, travel logistics, cancer risk, response timelines, and possible hormone therapy; the user said the discussion gave them a useful question list and lowered their anxiety. No safety-critical moment was raised.
